payload.title: [sfu-media-7] No empty/weak shared-secret guard in P2P TURN and SFU nonce minting — empty secret yields forgeabl...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING sfu-media-7 (medium/crypto, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/p2p-media-plane.ts
LINES: 188-200

WHAT: P2PWebRTCAdapter.#buildIceServers computes credential = HMAC-SHA1(this.#turn.sharedSecret, username) with no validation that sharedSecret is non-empty/sufficiently strong (constructor at lines 103-108 stores it verbatim). Same for SfuMediaPlaneAdapter.#mintNonce using tokenSecret (sfu-media-plane.ts:126, 279-283) — no guard. If an operator wires turn:{sharedSecret:''} (or undefined coerced upstream), HMAC with an empty key produces a deterministic, attacker-reproducible MAC: anyone can forge valid coturn-REST TURN credentials (and the SFU nonce, were it ever verified). There is also no minimum-length check.

IMPACT: A misconfigured/empty TURN shared secret makes ephemeral TURN credentials trivially forgeable, letting an attacker mint long-lived relay credentials and abuse the TURN server (bandwidth amplification / open relay) and impersonate participants. Fails closed nowhere — it silently issues weak creds.

SUGGESTED FIX: Validate sharedSecret/tokenSecret in the constructors: reject empty and enforce a sane minimum length (e.g. >= 16-32 bytes), throwing MediaPlaneError at construction so misconfiguration fails fast instead of issuing forgeable creds.
